Will Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp be blocked without net neutrality?

They wouldn't be blocked necessarily - you'd just have to pay extra for them. Like cable. But that's not even the worst of it.

Currently the internet is content neutral which means all traffic is treated the same. Internet providers are basically dumb pipes that move data around. You get internet access the same way you get water or power.

What they want to do is remove that neutrality and allow them to charge on tiered content schemes like cable. You don't pay an extra per-month charge for refrigerator power or AC power, do you? That's what internet providers want.

Imagine a Basic Water package that includes Toilet and Sink service, but if you want your dishwasher hooked up you'll need to pay an extra $/month just for the hookup - then you'll still be paying for the water you use.

Instead of HBO and Cinemax, you'd have an extra $4.99 per month for your Facebook package, and $14.99 for a Gaming Package that gives you access to Steam and XBox Live.

This is considered terrible because it puts all the power back in the hands of the big companies again, who are already making disgusting amounts of profit on old networks that haven't been upgraded in a long, long time. Bandwidth caps, even for cell phones, are largely to drive profits and have nothing to do with the actual capacity of their network.

But the worst part is that losing net neutrality makes censorship effortless for (((them))) at all levels. That's pretty much what this is, is just profit-driven censorship. Currently anyone with any opinion whatsoever is treated equally, but if we lose net neutrality then people will become OK with only having access to small parts of the internet at a time.

Someone has an opinion you don't like, or facts you'd rather see buried? Suddenly they drop off the common internet 'packages' and there's no way to find them. They'll already have content-blocking tools built in, so that site just drops off the face of the 'net and nobody ever bothers to look.
